The build is green: **59 tests run, 0 failures, 0 errors**.

## Summary

I extended the business-day rule in `BusinessDay.java` to skip public holidays as well as weekends.

**Change** (`src/main/java/.../rest/function/owner/BusinessDay.java`):
- Added a fixed `PUBLIC_HOLIDAYS` set: `2026-01-01`, `2026-01-26`, `2026-04-25`, `2026-12-25`, `2026-12-28`.
- Added an `isBusinessDay` helper that treats Saturdays, Sundays, and any listed holiday as non-business.
- Rewrote `rollForward` from a fixed weekend-only jump to a loop that advances one day at a time until it lands on a non-holiday weekday.

The loop-based approach correctly handles chained cases — e.g. `2026-12-25` (Fri holiday) → skips Sat/Sun → `2026-12-28` (also a holiday) → rolls forward to `2026-12-29`.

The change is confined to `rollForward`, so `effective(...)` and its caller `BuildOwner` pick up the new behavior automatically. The new `Cp47Tests` (holiday-business-day invariant) and all existing tests pass.

- Added a fixed `PUBLIC_HOLIDAYS` set: `2026-01-01`, `2026-01-26`, `2026-04-25`, `2026-12-25`, `2026-12-28`.
- Added an `isBusinessDay` helper that treats Saturdays, Sundays, and any listed holiday as non-business.
- Rewrote `rollForward` from a fixed weekend-only jump to a loop that advances one day at a time until it lands on a non-holiday weekday.

The loop-based approach correctly handles chained cases — e.g. `2026-12-25` (Fri holiday) → skips Sat/Sun → `2026-12-28` (also a holiday) → rolls forward to `2026-12-29`.

The change is confined to `rollForward`, so `effective(...)` and its caller `BuildOwner` pick up the new behavior automatically. The new `Cp47Tests` (holiday-business-day invariant) and all existing tests pass.
